title: Strict compact-support tower transitions and the fixed Roos shift model
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R$, uniformizer $t$, and $A_n=R/t^n$ for $n\ge1$. For finite-type $k$-schemes $W$ work on the small pro-etale sites with $\widehat R_W=\lim_n(A_n)_W$ and the strict semilinear system category $\mathscr S_W$ (module sheaves $M_n$ over $(A_n)_W$ with compatible semilinear transition maps). Use its ordinary unbounded derived category, derived reduction $\mathcal R_W$, total limit $\mathcal L_W=R\lim\operatorname{Res}$, and actual adjunction $\mathcal R_W\dashv\mathcal L_W$ with unit $u$ and counit $e$ of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. System operations are inverse image $P_v$ for separated finite-type maps $v$, direct image $S_p$ for proper $p$, quasi-compact open extension $J_j$, and derived tensor, with the integral counterparts of [lem-sf-integral-compactification-system-realization]. Restrict input and intermediate systems to normalized systems with compatible etale-origin witnesses, bounded constructible cohomology and finite Tor amplitude in common finite intervals; integral inputs are derived complete and constructible. Use the fixed slotwise cochain shifts of [def-pur-integral-operation-shift-data], with the signed second tensor slot, and the K-injective strict-tower Roos model for total limit. Write $\chi_H:H(M[r])\to H(M)[r]$ for a designated slot, holding other slots fixed. Let $f:X\to W$ be separated finite type, fix a compactification $f=pj$ with $j:X\hookrightarrow\overline X$ quasi-compact open and $p:\overline X\to W$ proper, and let $K$ be an allowed integral input. Choose a K-flat strict reduction model for $\mathcal RK$ and simultaneous models for $J_j$ and $S_p$. Write $U_W$ for termwise restriction from $(A_n)_W$-modules to $\widehat R_W$-modules, and put $T_K=U_WS_pJ_j\mathcal RK$, a strict tower complex.
The tower $T_K$ represents the inverse system defining the integral compact-support functor in [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]. More precisely its transition from $m$ to $n$ is $Rp_{*,m}j_!$ of the reduction map, followed by the canonical coefficient-restriction isomorphism of [lem-sf-compact-support-restriction-of-scalars]; this agreement includes the actual transition maps and compact-support structural maps. The specified comparison $c_{S_pJ_j}$ identifies $\mathcal L S_pJ_j\mathcal RK$ with that integral functor and its maps. Under this identification, the source total-limit shift obtained from the functorial K-injective strict-tower Roos representative is exactly the completed integral compact-support shift defined by termwise cochain shift of $T_K$ and its shifted-cone comparison. This equality of the two natural shift comparisons holds for every integer $r$, compatibly with zero, addition and inverses, and with the proper/open composite interpretation of compact support. No selection of a cone on a diagram of derived-category objects is made.

proof.text: Choose the single K-flat reduction representative in the statement. By the evaluation calculus its level $n$ is $K_n$ and its restriction-form transition $a_{m,n}:K_m\to\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}K_n$ is the actual quotient map. Exact termwise $J_j$ carries this to $j_!a_{m,n}$. Apply the pushforward-transition formula with $u=p$, $B_n=(A_n)_W$ and $N=J_j\mathcal RK$: the transition of $S_pN$ is $\delta_{m,n,N_n}\circ Rp_{*,m}(j_!a_{m,n})$. The compact-support scalar-restriction comparison is exactly this $\delta$ composed with the termwise open identification. After $U_W$, restriction along $\widehat R_W\to(A_m)_W\to(A_n)_W$ equals restriction directly to $(A_n)_W$. Thus these are precisely the transitions in the defining integral compact-support tower, for all $m\ge n$, including identities and composite transitions.

proof.text: Take $V=S_pJ_j$ in the simultaneous realization theorem. Its $V_{\mathrm{int}}$ is exactly the specified integral compact-support functor, and $\mathcal L_WV\mathcal RK=R\lim T_K$. Hence its specified $c_V$ identifies these functors. The same theorem intertwines open maps, units, counits, compositors and proper/open interchange, also in expression contexts. Consequently the identification includes the compact-support structural maps themselves and the proper/open composite, rather than just the evaluated objects. The assumed normalization, compatible etale-origin witnesses and common finite bounds are precisely its hypotheses for every intermediate system.

proof.text: Resolve the actual strict tower $T_K$ by the K-injective tower model of the injective-tower Roos-shift lemma. With $P=\prod_n I_n$ and $h=1-s$, its comparison is the localized kernel inclusion $\eta:\lim I_n\to C(I)=\operatorname{Cone}(h)[-1]$, $z\mapsto(0,(z_n))$. The lemma gives the natural chain isomorphism $C(I[r])\to C(I)[r]$, $(y,x)\mapsto((-1)^r y,x)$, and the equality $\chi_{I,r}\eta_{I[r]}=\eta_I[r]$. Therefore the source total-limit shift is the shifted-cone comparison on this actual tower, with its actual projections. The fixed operation-shift data identifies this total-limit comparison with the termwise product/cone comparison on every normalized Roos bridge and every termwise shifted representative, explicitly including $S_pJ_j\mathcal RK$. Thus this identification uses no exactness of products of arbitrary module sheaves and no cone chosen in a category of derived diagrams.

proof.text: For completeness compare the shifts through the specified $c_V$ itself. The realization recursion reads $c_{S_pJ_j}=S_{p,\mathrm{int}}(c_{J_j})\circ a_{S_p}(J_j\mathcal RK)$ and $c_{J_j}=J_{j,\mathrm{int}}(u_K^{-1})\circ a_{J_j}(\mathcal RK)$. The insertion-shift lemma gives the shift square for each $a$ and $u_K^{-1}$. Substitute these three squares in the two displayed composites: at each shared intermediate object the adjacent shift comparisons cancel, leaving $\chi_{(S_pJ_j)_{\mathrm{int}}}\circ c_{S_pJ_j}(K[r])=c_{S_pJ_j}(K)[r]\circ\chi_{\mathcal LS_pJ_j\mathcal R}$. This proves equality with the integral proper/open composite shift fixed in the operation-shift data. Step 3 identifies its total-limit factor with the required shifted-cone formula. All comparisons are natural for whole-system maps. The cited insertion and Roos lemmas hold for every integer and obey the zero and addition laws; the same laws survive composition and cancellation. In particular $(-1)^{r+s}=(-1)^r(-1)^s$ and $(-1)^{-r}=(-1)^r$ give zero, successive and inverse shifts with the same cone normalization.
